title: द्विषष्टितमोऽध्यायः
titleEn: Adhyaya 62 · Dhritarashtra's sons fall to Bhima

summary.en: With Duhshasana dead, ten of Dhritarashtra's sons attack Bhima in fury, and Bhima kills them one after another. Nakula strikes Karna's army, and Karna's son Vrishasena is wounded and carried off.
summary.kn: ದುಃಶಾಸನ ಸತ್ತ ಮೇಲೆ ಧೃತರಾಷ್ಟ್ರನ ಹತ್ತು ಮಕ್ಕಳು ಕೋಪದಿಂದ ಭೀಮನ ಮೇಲೆ ಎರಗುತ್ತಾರೆ; ಭೀಮ ಒಬ್ಬೊಬ್ಬರನ್ನೇ ಕೊಲ್ಲುತ್ತಾನೆ. ನಕುಲ ಕರ್ಣನ ಸೈನ್ಯದ ಮೇಲೆ ಎರಗುತ್ತಾನೆ; ಕರ್ಣನ ಮಗ ವೃಷಸೇನ ಗಾಯಗೊಂಡು ಒಯ್ಯಲ್ಪಡುತ್ತಾನೆ.
summary.hi: दुःशासन के मरने पर धृतराष्ट्र के दस पुत्र क्रोध से भीम पर टूटते हैं, और भीम उन्हें एक-एक कर मार देते हैं। नकुल कर्ण की सेना पर आक्रमण करता है और कर्ण का पुत्र वृषसेन घायल होकर ले जाया जाता है।
summary.te: దుశ్శాసనుడు చనిపోయాక ధృతరాష్ట్రుని పది మంది కుమారులు కోపంతో భీమునిపై దూకుతారు; భీముడు వారిని ఒకరి తరువాత ఒకరిని చంపుతాడు. నకులుడు కర్ణుని సేనపై దాడి చేస్తాడు; కర్ణుని కుమారుడు వృషసేనుడు గాయపడి తీసుకెళ్లబడతాడు.
summary.ta: துச்சாசனன் இறந்ததும் திருதராஷ்டிரனின் பத்து மக்கள் சினத்துடன் பீமனைத் தாக்க, பீமன் அவர்களை ஒருவர் பின் ஒருவராகக் கொல்கிறான். நகுலன் கர்ணனின் படையைத் தாக்க, கர்ணனின் மகன் விருஷசேனன் காயமுற்றுக் கொண்டு செல்லப்படுகிறான்.
summary.ml: ദുശ്ശാസനൻ വീണശേഷം, ധൃതരാഷ്ട്രപുത്രന്മാരിൽ പത്തുപേർ കോപത്തോടെ ഭീമനെ ആക്രമിക്കുന്നു; ഭീമൻ അവരെ ഓരോരുത്തരെയായി കൊല്ലുന്നു. നകുലൻ കർണ്ണന്റെ സേനയെ പ്രഹരിക്കുന്നു; കർണ്ണന്റെ പുത്രൻ വൃഷസേനന് മുറിവേറ്റ് അദ്ദേഹത്തെ കൊണ്ടുപോകുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 8.62; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Mon Jul 29 2019

verses.text: संजय उवाच

meaning.en: Sanjaya said:

verses.text:
दुःशासने तु निहते पुत्रास्तव महारथाः ।
महाक्रोधविषा वीराः समरेष्वपलायिनः ।
दश राजन्महावीर्यो भीमं प्राच्छादयञ्शरैः ॥

meaning.en: When Duhshasana was slain, your mighty sons, heroes with the poison of great anger who never fled in battle, ten of them of great strength, O king, covered Bhima with arrows.

verses.text:
कवची निषङ्गी पाशी दण्डधारो धनुर्धरः ।
अलोलुपः शलः संधो वातवेगसुवर्चसौ ॥

meaning.en: They were Kavachi, Nishangi, Pashi, Dandadhara, Dhanurdhara, Alolupa, Shala, Sandha, and the two Vatavega and Suvarchas.

verses.text:
एते समेत्य सहिता भ्रातृव्यसनकर्शिताः ।
भीमसेनं महाबाहुं मार्गणैः समवारयन् ॥

meaning.en: Coming together, tormented by grief for their brother, they held back the mighty-armed Bhimasena with their arrows.

verses.text:
स वार्यमाणो विशिखैः समन्तात्तैर्महारथैः ।
भीमः क्रोधाभिरक्ताक्षः क्रुद्धः काल इवाबभौ ॥

meaning.en: Held back on all sides by those great chariot-warriors with their shafts, Bhima, his eyes red with fury, looked like Time in his anger.

verses.text:
तांस्तु भल्लैर्महावेगैर्दशभिर्दशभिः शितैः ।
रुक्माङ्गदो रुक्मपुङ्खैः पार्थो निन्ये यमक्षयम् ॥

meaning.en: The Pandava Partha, wearing a golden armlet, sent them to Yama's abode, ten by ten, with sharp, swift, gold-feathered broad-headed arrows.

verses.text:
हतेषु तेषु वीरेषु प्रदुद्राव बलं तव ।
पश्यतः सूतपुत्रस्य पाण्डवस्य भयार्दितम् ॥

meaning.en: When those heroes were slain, your army, stricken with fear of the Pandava, fled before the eyes of the charioteer's son.

verses.text:
ततः कर्णो महाराज प्रविवेश महारणम् ।
दृष्ट्वा भीमस्य विक्रान्तमन्तकस्य प्रजास्विव ॥

meaning.en: Then, great king, Karna entered the great battle, seeing Bhima's prowess, like Death's among living creatures.

verses.text:
तस्य त्वाकारभावज्ञः शल्यः समितिशोभनः ।
उवाच वचनं कर्णं प्राप्तकालमरिंदम ।
मा व्यथां कुरु राधेय नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते ॥

meaning.en: Shalya, who understood the look and mood of Karna and was a glory of assemblies, spoke words suited to the moment, O tamer of foes: "Do not be troubled, son of Radha; this does not become you.

verses.text:
एते द्रवन्ति राजानो भीमसेनभयार्दिताः ।
दुर्योधनश्च संमूढो भ्रातृव्यसनदुःखितः ॥

meaning.en: These kings are fleeing, tormented by fear of Bhimasena, and Duryodhana is bewildered and pained by his brothers' deaths.

verses.text:
दुःशासनस्य रुधिरे पीयमाने महात्मना ।
व्यापन्नचेतसश्चैव शोकोपहतमन्यवः ॥

meaning.en: When the great-souled Bhima drank Duhshasana's blood, their minds were shattered and their anger overcome by grief.

verses.text:
दुर्योधनमुपासन्ते परिवार्य समन्ततः ।
कृपप्रभृतयः कर्ण हतशेषाश्च सोदराः ॥

meaning.en: Kripa and the others, and the remaining brothers who survived, stand all around Duryodhana and attend him.

verses.text:
पाण्डवा लब्धलक्षाश्च धनंजयपुरोगमाः ।
त्वामेवाभिमुखाः शूरा युद्धाय समुपास्थिताः ॥

meaning.en: The Pandavas, who have got their chance, led by Dhananjaya, stand ready for battle, heroes facing you alone.

verses.text:
स त्वं पुरुषशार्दूल पौरुषे महति स्थितः ।
क्षत्रधर्मं पुरस्कृत्य प्रत्युद्याहि धनंजयम् ॥

meaning.en: So you, tiger among men, standing in great manliness and giving first place to your warrior's duty, go forth against Dhananjaya.

verses.text:
भारो हि धार्तराष्ट्रेण त्वयि सर्वः समर्पितः ।
तमुद्वह महाबाहो यथाशक्ति यथाबलम् ।
जये स्याद्विपुला कीर्तिर्ध्रुवः स्वर्गः पराजये ॥

meaning.en: Dhritarashtra's son has laid the whole burden on you. Bear it, mighty-armed one, as best you can and with all your strength: if you win, great fame; if you are defeated, heaven is certain.

verses.text:
वृषसेनश्च राधेय संक्रुद्धस्तनयस्तव ।
त्वयि मोहसमापन्ने पाण्डवानभिधावति ॥

meaning.en: And your son Vrishasena, son of Radha, is furious and is rushing at the Pandavas while you are in a daze."

verses.text:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु वचनं शल्यस्यामिततेजसः ।
हृदि मानुष्यकं भावं चक्रे युद्धाय सुस्थिरम् ॥

meaning.en: Hearing these words of the boundlessly powerful Shalya, Karna firmed up his human feeling in his heart for the fight.

verses.text:
ततः क्रुद्धो वृषसेनोऽभ्यधाव-
दातस्थिवांसं स्वरथं हतारिम् ।
वृकोदरं कालमिवात्तदण्डं
गदाहस्तं पोथमानं त्वदीयान् ॥

meaning.en: Then the enraged Vrishasena ran at Vrikodara, who stood on his own chariot, having killed his enemies, mace in hand like Death with his rod, and crushing your men.

verses.text:
तमभ्यधावन्नकुलः प्रवीरो
रोषादमित्रं प्रतुदन्पृषत्कैः ।
कर्णस्य पुत्रं समरे प्रहृष्टं
जिष्णुर्जिघांसुर्मघवेव जम्भम् ॥

meaning.en: The heroic Nakula, tormenting that enemy with arrows in his rage, ran at him, Karna's son, exulting in the battle, as victorious Indra with Maghavan's fury ran at Jambha, wishing to kill him.

verses.text:
ततो ध्वजं स्फाटिकचित्रकम्बुं
चिच्छेद वीरो नकुलः क्षुरेण ।
कर्णात्मजस्येष्वसनं च चित्रं
भल्लेन जाम्बूनदपट्टनद्धम् ॥

meaning.en: Then the hero Nakula cut with a razor-headed arrow the banner of Karna's son, a splendid one with a crystal-colored conch, and with a broad-headed arrow his fine bow, bound in gold bands.

verses.text:
अथान्यदादाय धनुः सुशीघ्रं
कर्णात्मजः पाण्डवमभ्यविध्यत् ।
दिव्यैर्महास्त्रैर्नकुलं महास्त्रो
दुःशासनस्यापचितिं यियासुः ॥

meaning.en: Then Karna's son, taking another bow very quickly, pierced the Pandava Nakula, being himself skilled in great weapons, with divine great missiles, wishing to take vengeance for Duhshasana.

verses.text:
ततः क्रुद्धो नकुलस्तं महात्मा
शरैर्महोल्काप्रतिमैरविध्यत् ।
दिव्यैरस्त्रैरभ्यविध्यच्च सोऽपि
कर्णस्य पुत्रो नकुलं कृतास्त्रः ॥

meaning.en: Then the great-souled Nakula, enraged, pierced him with arrows like huge meteors, and Karna's son, trained in weapons, pierced Nakula too with divine missiles.

verses.text:
कर्णस्य पुत्रो नकुलस्य राज-
न्सर्वानश्वानक्षिणोदुत्तमास्त्रैः ।
वनायुजान्सुकुमारस्य शुभ्रा-
नलंकृताञ्जातरूपेण शीघ्रान् ॥

meaning.en: O king, Karna's son destroyed all the horses of Nakula, the delicate prince, with his best missiles: white, swift horses from Vanayu, adorned with gold.

verses.text:
ततो हताश्वादवरुह्य याना-
दादाय चर्म रुचिरं चाष्टचन्द्रम् ।
आकाशसंकाशमसिं गृहीत्वा
पोप्लूयमानः खगवच्चचार ॥

meaning.en: Then Nakula, with his horses slain, got down from the chariot, took a fine shield marked with eight moons and a sword shining like the sky, and moved about leaping like a bird.

verses.text:
ततोऽन्तरिक्षे नृवराश्वनागां-
श्चिच्छेद मार्गान्विचरन्विचित्रान् ।
ते प्रापतन्नसिना गां विशस्ता
यथाश्वमेधे पशवः शमित्रा ॥

meaning.en: Then, moving along strange paths in mid-air, he cut down choice men, horses and elephants; slain by his sword, they fell to earth like sacrificial animals at an Ashvamedha, killed by the officiating priest.

verses.text:
द्विसाहस्रा विदिता युद्धशौण्डा
नानादेश्याः सुभृताः सत्यसंधाः ।
एकेन शीघ्रं नकुलेन कृत्ताः
सारेप्सुनेवोत्तमचन्दनास्ते ॥

meaning.en: Two thousand known warriors, skilled in battle, from many lands, well supported and true to their word, were cut down swiftly by Nakula alone, like trees of the best sandalwood by a man who wants the heartwood.

verses.text:
तमापतन्तं नकुलं सोऽभिपत्य
समन्ततः सायकैरभ्यविध्यत् ।
स तुद्यमानो नकुलः पृषत्कै-
र्विव्याध वीरं स चुकोप विद्धः ॥

meaning.en: Karna's son fell upon that Nakula as he came on and pierced him from every side with arrows; Nakula, tormented by the shafts, pierced the hero in return, and that one, wounded, grew angry.

verses.text:
तं कर्णपुत्रो विधमन्तमेकं
नराश्वमातङ्गरथप्रवेकान् ।
क्रीडन्तमष्टादशभिः पृषत्कै-
र्विव्याध वीरं स चुकोप विद्धः ॥

meaning.en: As Nakula, alone, was destroying the foremost men, horses, elephants and chariots, and playing at it, Karna's son pierced the hero with eighteen arrows, and being pierced, Nakula grew angry.

verses.text:
ततोऽभ्यधावत्समरे जिघांसुः
कर्णात्मजं पाण्डुसुतो नृवीरः ।
तस्येषुभिर्व्यधमत्कर्णपुत्रो
महारणे चर्म सहस्रतारम् ॥

meaning.en: Then the Pandava hero ran at Karna's son in the battle, wishing to kill him; but Karna's son shattered with his arrows Nakula's shield, set with a thousand stars, in the great fight.

verses.text:
तस्यायसं निशितं तीक्ष्णधार-
मसिं विकोशं गुरुभारसाहम् ।
द्विषच्छरीरापहरं सुघोर-
माधुन्वतः सर्पमिवोग्ररूपम् ॥

meaning.en: Nakula was shaking his sharp, iron, keen-edged sword out of its sheath, a dreadful, fierce-looking thing like a snake, able to bear great weight and to take the lives of enemies.

verses.text:
क्षिप्रं शरैः षड्भिरमित्रसाह-
श्चकर्त खड्गं निशितैः सुधारैः ।
पुनश्च पीतैर्निशितैः पृषत्कैः
स्तनान्तरे गाढमथाभ्यविध्यत् ॥

meaning.en: The enemy-conqueror Vrishasena quickly cut the sword with six sharp, well-edged arrows, and then pierced Nakula deeply between the breasts with more sharp, well-whetted arrows.

verses.text:
स भीमसेनस्य रथं हताश्वो
माद्रीसुतः कर्णसुताभितप्तः ।
आपुप्लुवे सिंह इवाचलाग्रं
संप्रेक्षमाणस्य धनंजयस्य ॥

meaning.en: Madri's son, with horses slain and tormented by Karna's son, leapt onto Bhimasena's chariot, like a lion onto a mountain peak, as Dhananjaya looked on.

verses.text:
नकुलमथ विदित्वा छिन्नबाणासनासिं
विरथमरिशरार्तं कर्णपुत्रास्त्रभग्नम् ।
पवनधुतपताका ह्रादिनो वल्गिताश्वा
वरपुरुषनियत्तास्ते रथाः शीघ्रमीयुः ॥

meaning.en: Knowing Nakula to be without his bow and sword, chariotless, pained by enemy arrows and broken by the missiles of Karna's son, the chariots, with flags fluttering in the wind, roaring, with horses prancing, were driven by their foremost men and hurried swiftly there.

verses.text:
द्रुपदसुतवरिष्ठाः पञ्च शैनेयषष्ठा
द्रुपददुहितृपुत्राः पञ्च चामित्रसाहाः ।
द्विरदरथनराश्वान्सूदयन्तस्त्वदीया-
न्भुजगपतिनिकाशैर्मार्गणैरात्तशस्त्राः ॥

meaning.en: The five chief sons of Drupada, with Satyaki as sixth, and the five sons of Drupada's daughter, enemy-conquerors, took up arms and slew your elephants, chariots, men and horses with arrows like lords of serpents.

verses.text:
अथ तव रथमुख्यास्तान्प्रतीयुस्त्वरन्तो
हृदिकसुतकृपौ च द्रौणिदुर्योधनौ च ।
शकुनिशुकवृकाश्च क्राथदेवावृधौ च
द्विरदजलदघोषैः स्यन्दनैः कार्मुकैश्च ॥

meaning.en: Then your foremost chariot-warriors, Kritavarman, Kripa, Drona's son, Duryodhana, Shakuni, Shuka, Vrika, Kratha and Devavridha, hastened toward them in chariots that rumbled like elephants and clouds, with bows in hand.

verses.text:
तव नरवरवर्यास्तान्दशैकं च वीरा-
न्प्रवरशरवराग्र्यैस्ताडयन्तोऽभ्यरुन्धन् ।
नवजलदसवर्णैर्हस्तिभिस्तानुदीयु-
र्गिरिशिखरनिकाशैर्भीमवेगैः कुणिन्दाः ॥

meaning.en: Your best of heroes, striking them with their finest arrows, ten and one in number, held them back; and the Kunindas rose against them on elephants dark as new rain clouds, like mountain peaks and terrible in speed.

verses.text:
सुकल्पिता हैमवता मदोत्कटा
रणाभिकामैः कृतिभिः समास्थिताः ।
सुवर्णजालावतता बभुर्गजा-
स्तथा यथा वै जलदाः सविद्युतः ॥

meaning.en: Those Himalayan elephants, well equipped and wild with rut, mounted by skilled men eager for battle, shone with their golden nets like clouds with lightning.

verses.text:
कुणिन्दपुत्रो दशभिर्महायसैः
कृपं ससूताश्वमपीडयद्भृशम् ।
ततः शरद्वत्सुतसायकैर्हतः
सहैव नागेन पपात भूतले ॥

meaning.en: The Kunindas' prince struck Kripa hard with ten great iron arrows, with his charioteer and horses; then, killed by the arrows of Sharadvat's son, he fell to the ground with his elephant.

verses.text:
कुणिन्दपुत्रावरजस्तु तोमरै-
र्दिवाकरांशुप्रतिमैरयस्मयैः ।
रथं च विक्षोभ्य ननाद नर्दत-
स्ततोऽस्य गान्धारपतिः शिरोऽहरत् ॥

meaning.en: The Kunindas' prince's younger brother, with iron javelins like the sun's rays, shook Kripa's chariot and roared; then the lord of Gandhara cut off his head.

verses.text:
ततः कुणिन्देषु हतेषु तेष्वथ
प्रहृष्टरूपास्तव ते महारथाः ।
भृशं प्रदध्मुर्लवणाम्बुसंभवा-
न्परांश्च बाणासनपाणयोऽभ्ययुः ॥

meaning.en: When those Kunindas were slain, your great chariot-warriors, delighted, blew their conches born of the salt sea loudly and advanced on their enemies with bows in hand.

verses.text:
अथाभवद्युद्धमतीव दारुणं
पुनः कुरूणां सह पाण्डुसृञ्जयैः ।
शरासिशक्त्यृष्टिगदापरश्वधै-
र्नराश्वनागासुहरं भृशाकुलम् ॥

meaning.en: Then a very dreadful battle began again between the Kurus and the Pandavas with the Srinjayas, with arrows, swords, darts, spears, maces and axes, taking the lives of men, horses and elephants, and thick with confusion.

verses.text:
रथाश्वमातङ्गपदातिभिस्ततः
परस्परं विप्रहतापतन्क्षितौ ।
यथा सविद्युत्स्तनिता बलाहकाः
समास्थिता दिग्भ्य इवोग्रमारुतैः ॥

meaning.en: Struck down by chariots, horses, elephants and foot soldiers, men fell to the ground, like clouds with lightning and thunder driven together from all quarters by fierce winds.

verses.text:
ततः शतानीकहतान्महागजां-
स्तथा रथान्पत्तिगणांश्च तावकान् ।
जघान भोजश्च हयानथापत-
न्विशस्त्रकृत्ताः कृतवर्मणा द्विपाः ॥

meaning.en: Then Shatanika killed your great elephants, chariots and troops of foot soldiers, while Kritavarman the Bhoja killed horses, and elephants fell with their weapons cut away.

verses.text:
अथापरे द्रौणिशराहता द्विपा-
स्त्रयः ससर्वायुधयोधकेतवः ।
निपेतुरुर्व्यां व्यसवः प्रपातिता-
स्तथा यथा वज्रहता महाचलाः ॥

meaning.en: Three more elephants, struck by Drona's son's arrows, with all their weapons, warriors and banners, fell lifeless to the ground, like great mountains struck by thunderbolts.

verses.text:
कुणिन्दराजावरजादनन्तरः
स्तनान्तरे पत्रिवरैरताडयत् ।
तवात्मजं तस्य तवात्मजः शरैः
शितैः शरीरं बिभिदे द्विपं च तम् ॥

meaning.en: Next after the Kunindas' king's younger brother, your son struck Duryodhana's son between the breasts with fine arrows; Duryodhana's son pierced that man's body, and his elephant too, with sharp arrows.

verses.text:
स नागराजः सह राजसूनुना
पपात रक्तं बहु सर्वतः क्षरन् ।
शचीशवज्रप्रहतोऽम्बुदागमे
यथा जलं गैरिकपर्वतस्तथा ॥

meaning.en: That king of elephants fell with the prince, streaming blood on every side, like a mountain of red ochre, struck by Indra's thunderbolt in the rainy season, streaming water.

verses.text:
कुणिन्दपुत्रप्रहितोऽपरद्विपः
शुकं ससूताश्वरथं व्यपोथयत् ।
ततोऽपतत्क्राथशराभिदारितः
सहेश्वरो वज्रहतो यथा गिरिः ॥

meaning.en: Another elephant, driven on by a Kunindas prince, crushed Shuka with his charioteer, horses and chariot; then it fell, torn by Kratha's arrows, like a mountain struck by Indra's thunderbolt.

verses.text:
रथी द्विपस्थेन हतोऽपतच्छरैः
क्राथाधिपः पर्वतजेन दुर्जयः ।
सवाजिसूतेष्वसनस्तथापत-
द्यथा महावातहतो महाद्रुमः ॥

meaning.en: The invincible lord of the Krathas, a chariot-warrior, was struck by arrows and killed by a warrior born in the mountains, mounted on an elephant; he fell with horses, charioteer and bow, like a great tree broken by a mighty wind.

verses.text:
वृको द्विपस्थं गिरिराजवासिनं
भृशं शरैर्द्वादशभिः पराभिनत् ।
ततो वृकं साश्वरथं महाजवं
त्वरंश्चतुर्भिश्चरणे व्यपोथयत् ॥

meaning.en: Vrika pierced hard with twelve arrows the mountain-dweller riding the elephant; then he quickly crushed Vrika, with his horses and chariot of great speed, with four arrows at the feet.

verses.text:
स नागराजः सनियन्तृकोऽपत-
त्पराहतो बभ्रुसुतेषुभिर्भृशम् ।
स चापि देवावृधसूनुरर्दितः
पपात नुन्नः सहदेवसूनुना ॥

meaning.en: That king of elephants fell with its driver, badly struck by the arrows of Babhru's son; and the son of Devavridha too fell, tormented and driven down by the son of Sahadeva.

verses.text:
विषाणपोत्रापरगात्रघातिना
गजेन हन्तुं शकुनेः कुणिन्दजः ।
जगाम वेगेन भृशार्दयंश्च तं
ततोऽस्य गान्धारपतिः शिरोऽहरत् ॥

meaning.en: A Kunindas man went swiftly on an elephant that smashed the limbs of others with its tusk and trunk, to kill Shakuni, tormenting him hard; then the lord of Gandhara cut off his head.

verses.text:
ततः शतानीकहता महागजा
हया रथाः पत्तिगणाश्च तावकाः ।
सुपर्णवातप्रहता यथा नगा-
स्तथा गता गामवशा विचूर्णिताः ॥

meaning.en: Then your great elephants, horses, chariots and troops of foot soldiers, struck by Shatanika, were crushed and fell helpless to the ground, like trees struck by the wind of Garuda.

verses.text:
ततोऽभ्यविध्यद्बहुभिः शितैः शरैः
कुणिन्दपुत्रो नकुलात्मजं स्मयन् ।
ततोऽस्य कायान्निचकर्त नाकुलिः
शिरः क्षुरेणाम्बुजसंनिभाननम् ॥

meaning.en: Then the Kunindas' prince, smiling, pierced Nakula's son with many sharp arrows; but Nakula's son cut off, with a razor-headed arrow, his head with its lotus-like face from his body.

verses.text:
ततः शतानीकमविध्यदाशुगै-
स्त्रिभिः शितैः कर्णसुतोऽर्जुनं त्रिभिः ।
त्रिभिश्च भीमं नकुलं च सप्तभि-
र्जनार्दनं द्वादशभिश्च सायकैः ॥

meaning.en: Then Karna's son pierced Shatanika with three swift sharp arrows, Arjuna with three, Bhima with three, Nakula with seven, and Janardana with twelve.

verses.text:
तदस्य कर्मातिमनुष्यकर्मणः
समीक्ष्य हृष्टाः कुरवोऽभ्यपूजयन् ।
पराक्रमज्ञास्तु धनंजयस्य ते
हुतोऽयमग्नाविति तं तु मेनिरे ॥

meaning.en: Seeing that deed of his, beyond human power, the delighted Kurus honored him; but those who knew Dhananjaya's prowess thought, "He has been offered into the fire."

verses.text:
ततः किरीटी परवीरघाती
हताश्वमालोक्य नरप्रवीरम् ।
तमभ्यधावद्वृषसेनमाहवे
स सूतजस्य प्रमुखे स्थितं तदा ॥

meaning.en: Then the diadem-wearer, slayer of enemy heroes, seeing the hero of men Nakula left without horses, ran in the battle at Vrishasena, who then stood before the charioteer's son.

verses.text:
तमापतन्तं नरवीरमुग्रं
महाहवे बाणसहस्रधारिणम् ।
अभ्यापतत्कर्णसुतो महारथो
यथैव चेन्द्रं नमुचिः पुरातने ॥

meaning.en: As that fierce hero among men, wielding a thousand arrows, charged in the great fight, the great chariot-warrior, Karna's son, rushed at him, as Namuchi did at Indra in ancient times.

verses.text:
ततोऽद्भुतेनैकशतेन पार्थं
शरैर्विद्ध्वा सूतपुत्रस्य पुत्रः ।
ननाद नादं सुमहानुभावो
विद्ध्वेव शक्रं नमुचिः पुरा वै ॥

meaning.en: Then the son of the charioteer's son, of great power, pierced Partha with a marvelous hundred and one arrows and roared a cry, as Namuchi did long ago after wounding Indra.

verses.text:
पुनः स पार्थं वृषसेन उग्रै-
र्बाणैरविध्यद्भुजमूलमध्ये ।
तथैव कृष्णं नवभिः समार्दय-
त्पुनश्च पार्थं दशभिः शिताग्रैः ॥

meaning.en: Vrishasena again pierced Partha with fierce arrows at the base of his arm, struck Krishna with nine, and again Partha with ten sharp-tipped arrows.

verses.text:
ततः किरीटी रणमूर्ध्नि कोपा-
त्कृत्वा त्रिशाखां भ्रुकुटिं ललाटे ।
मुमोच बाणान्विशिखान्महात्मा
वधाय राजन्सूतपुत्रस्य संख्ये ॥

meaning.en: Then the great-souled diadem-wearer, in anger at the head of the battle, drew his brow into three furrows on his forehead and loosed his arrows to kill the charioteer's son in the fight, O king.

verses.text:
विव्याध चैनं दशभिः पृषत्कै-
र्मर्मस्वसक्तं प्रसभं किरीटी ।
चिच्छेद चास्येष्वसनं भुजौ च
क्षुरैश्चतुर्भिः शिर एव चोग्रैः ॥

meaning.en: The diadem-wearer forcibly pierced him with ten arrows, which clung to his vital parts, and cut his bow and his arms, and with four fierce razor-headed arrows his head too.

verses.text:
स पार्थबाणाभिहतः पपात
रथाद्विबाहुर्विशिरा धरायाम् ।
सुपुष्पितः पर्णधरोऽतिकायो
वातेरितः शाल इवाद्रिशृङ्गात् ॥

meaning.en: Struck by Partha's arrows, Vrishasena fell from his chariot to the ground, without arms and without head, like a tall, blossoming, leafy sal tree blown from a mountain peak by the wind.

verses.text:
तं प्रेक्ष्य बाणाभिहतं पतन्तं
रथात्सुतं सूतजः क्षिप्रकारी ।
रथं रथेनाशु जगाम वेगा-
त्किरीटिनः पुत्रवधाभितप्तः ॥

meaning.en: Seeing his son struck by arrows and falling from the chariot, Karna the charioteer's son, who acts swiftly, burned with grief at his son's death and drove his chariot swiftly against the diadem-wearer's.
